Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/UpdateGate.tsx:43 and /app/frontend/app/_layout.tsx (import chain).

critical_code_review_comments: src/components/UpdateGate.tsx:43 — `const mod = require("sp-react-native-in-app-updates");` is inside `useEffect > run()` guarded by `Platform.OS !== 'android'` early-return, BUT Metro still statically analyses the require() call, and the package has NO .web.js sibling — so the web bundle CANNOT be built. Runtime-only guards do not protect against static resolver errors. Platform-specific sibling files (UpdateGate.web.tsx) are the idiomatic Expo fix. This is exactly the class of bug that iter19 called out (RN issues to always flag).

rca_of_issue: RCA — v1.0.17 web bundle blank screen. Bug: UpdateGate.tsx uses `require("sp-react-native-in-app-updates")` inside useEffect, guarded by `Platform.OS !== 'android' return`. Metro bundler performs STATIC dependency graph analysis regardless of runtime guards; it walks the require() at bundle time and tries to resolve the package's index.js, which does `require("./InAppUpdates")`. That target only exists as .android.js / .ios.js siblings — for platform=web there is no matching file → Metro reports 'Unable to resolve ./InAppUpdates from node_modules/sp-react-native-in-app-updates/lib/commonjs/index.js' → bundle build fails → dev server returns 500 for entry.bundle → web renders the fallback 'You need to enable JavaScript to run this app' HTML with no React tree. Repro: cd /app/frontend && expo start --port 3000 --web (before fix) → tail /var/log/supervisor/expo.out.log shows the error, curl http://localhost:3000/_expo/static/js/web/entry.bundle returns 500. Mitigation applied: created UpdateGate.web.tsx which Metro's platform-extensions resolver picks first on web, so UpdateGate.tsx (with the failing require) is never included in the web bundle. Result: web bundle builds in ~3.4 s, root layout mounts, home renders, punch E2E completes in ~6 s to /attendance/result. No changes to metro.config.js, app.json, or babel.config.js.
